title: One Sequence Is Enough: Fingerprinting Language Models from Fixed-Length Integer Sequences
abstract: arXiv:2611.14010v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Users of model APIs and third-party platforms often rely on the declared model name to identify the model responding to their requests. However, the actual model may differ from the declared one, motivating identity verification based on observable outputs. Previous studies have shown that preferences in simple numerical-choice tasks can serve as model fingerprints. We investigate whether a single fixed-length integer sequence can combine multiple numerical observations to identify its source model. For this task, we introduce NumPrint, a benchmark of 5,036 answers from 51 models, collected using Chinese, Japanese, and English prompts that request 294 integers between 1 and 355 in one response. We propose the Shallow MLP and Causal Transformer (SMCT) to capture aggregate numerical preferences and behavioral patterns in generated sequences. translated_title: 一个序列就足够了：从定长整数序列对语言模型进行指纹识别
translated_abstract: 模型API和第三方平台的用户通常依赖所声明的模型名称来识别响应其请求的模型。然而，实际模型可能与声明的模型不符，这促使人们需要基于可观测输出的身份验证方法。先前的研究表明，简单数字选择任务中的偏好可以作为模型指纹。我们研究单个定长整数序列能否结合多个数值观测来识别其来源模型。为此，我们提出了NumPrint基准，其中包含来自51个模型的5,036个答案，这些答案是使用中文、日文和英文提示收集的，提示要求模型在一次响应中给出294个1到355之间的整数。我们提出了浅层MLP与因果Transformer（SMCT）来捕捉生成序列中的整体数值偏好和行为模式。在51类闭集评估中，SMCT仅凭单个序列即可达到92.72%的准确率，优于现有基线方法。
tldr: 该论文提出NumPrint基准和SMCT模型，证明仅凭模型生成的一条定长整数序列，就能以92.72%的准确率在51个语言模型中识别出响应请求的真实模型。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes the NumPrint benchmark and the SMCT model, showing that a single fixed-length integer sequence generated by a language model can identify its source model among 51 models with 92.72% accuracy.
